messages:
jane_customer: Hi, trying to sign in with Google from our Android app and getting redirected back to /auth/callback with a 403. Works in desktop Chrome, fails behind our proxy/when hitting staging URL. Can share logs.

emily_support: Sorry you're stuck — can you paste the redirect URL you're seeing and the exact error body? Also which flow: PKCE or implicit?

jane_customer: It's PKCE (code + state). Redirect looks like: https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=4/0AX4XfW...&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

emily_support: thx. Any chance the state or code look truncated? Mobile webview + reverse proxies sometimes chop long query params. Can you dump the callback query string from server logs?

jane_customer: here's the raw logger line from our callback handler: 
```
GET /auth/callback?code=4/0AX4XfWbhqz...&state=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFjdGlvbl9sb25nX3N0YXRlX2Zvcl90ZXN0X3VybF9zaGFyZWRfc3RyaW5nX3dpdGhfY29tbWFzIn0%3D HTTP/1.1
Host: app.example.com
User-Agent: okhttp/4.9.3
```

emily_support: looks like the state ends with %3D which is => '=' (base64 padding). If proxy or app double-decodes or trims, that could break the HMAC verification.

jane_customer: We compare the state param to what's in the session cookie and it doesn't match. Session cookie has full state base64 with trailing '='; request has URL-encoded version.

devon_se: pinging @raj_infra — we saw a similar thing where AWS ALB + CloudFront dropped trailing '=' or truncated long query params for mobile deep links. Raj, any infra-side fixes?

raj_infra: looking — our ALB is fine but CloudFront had a rule that normalizes query strings and can drop certain chars during signed URL processing. Also some WAF rules limit query length. Can you share the exact state length?

jane_customer: state length ~340 chars (base64url). Not huge but includes '+' and '=' padding in some cases.

emily_support: common causes:
- URL encoding mismatch: ensure client uses encodeURIComponent for the state and server decodes once.
- Proxy trimming: check CloudFront/NGINX max_uri and query_string length (e.g., large_client_header_buffers or proxy_buffer_size).
- '+' vs ' ' issue: some proxies convert '+' to space if not encoded.

jane_customer: repro steps I used:
1) Android WebView opens https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?...&state=LONG_BASE64
2) Google redirects to our redirect_uri (app://callback -> deep link -> our backend gets real callback via https redirect)
3) Backend handler logs state and compares to session cookie -> mismatch 100% on device, works on desktop.

devon_se: can you try base64url (replace +/ with -_) and strip padding on both sides? Also we had cases where PKCE verifier length changes if client sends code_verifier with trailing padding removed. Server-side libs sometimes expect padding.

jane_customer: quick test: I changed the client to base64url without padding and server accepted it. But that's a workaround; want to understand root: why is mobile path different?

raj_infra: Checked CloudFront logs for those request IDs. Looks like the redirect URL passed through a proxy that rewrote the query: it percent-decoded, then re-encoded, and dropped trailing '=' in one chunk because of a URL-length normalization routine. I'll open a ticket with CDN team to disable that normalization for our callback path.

emily_support: in the meantime, two mitigation options: 1) support paddingless base64url on server and normalize state before checking, 2) move state into a short opaque ID stored in server-side session (short token < 64 chars) and avoid long query param.

jane_customer: Thanks — I'll implement server-side normalization + accept paddingless variant. Also will work with infra to patch CDN rule.

oauth-bot: Automatic alert: 5 failed /auth/callback verifications in last 10m for client: mobile-android, rule: state_mismatch.

emily_support: Thanks @jane_customer — once CDN rule is changed let us know and we can close. If you can paste a sanitized example of the before/after state values that'd help us update docs. :thumbsup:

jane_customer: Will do. Appreciate the quick help! :pray:
